title: Kafka as a Doctor of Law, around 1906 (Atelier Jacobi)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons (photographer: Atelier Jacobi / Sigismund Jacobi, 1860-1935)
licenseBasis: Photographer Sigismund Jacobi died 1935; life+70 protection expired 2006 (EU) and image predates 1930 US publication cutoff
notes: Only resolution available on Commons for this file (no higher-res version found despite file-page mentions of a Bodleian copy and other archives citing the same photo -- those are source citations, not alternate uploads). Bodleian's own digitization of this portrait is NOT used here due to unclear/likely non-commercial licensing; this Commons upload is a separately-sourced, PD-tagged scan.

title: Franz Kafka's Signature (vectorized)
sourceCollection: Wikimedia Commons (vector traced by user Jon C from a GIF sourced via projekt-gutenberg.org, c. 1913 signature)
licenseBasis: A mere signature is below the threshold of originality for copyright in Germany/US regardless of the signer's death date
notes: Vector format -- scales losslessly for the art pass.

title: Kafka's notebook -- German-Hebrew vocabulary page, Prague 1922 (autograph manuscript)
sourceCollection: National Library of Israel, Givat Ram, Jerusalem (Vessel to Vessel digital gallery)
licenseBasis: Author (Franz Kafka) died 1924; life+70 protection expired 1994
notes: This is Kafka's own handwriting (German/Hebrew vocabulary practice), not the Bodleian's Trial/Diaries holdings -- avoids the Bodleian license-uncertainty flagged in the brief. Considered but rejected: 'Franz Kafka - Drawings - Literary Estate Max Brod - National Library of Israel.jpg' (commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Franz_Kafka_-_Drawings_-_Literary_Estate_Max_Brod_-_National_Library_of_Israel.jpg) -- tagged CC-PD-Mark but is a 2019 press photo credited 'Photo by Menahem Kahana / AFP', so the photographic reproduction's own copyright status is murky even though the underlying drawing is PD; also low-res (278x444).

title: Die Verwandlung, 1st edition, original blue cardboard binding (Kurt Wolff Verlag, Leipzig, printed November 1915 as vol. 22/23 of 'Der jungste Tag')
sourceCollection: Antiquariat Dr. Haack Leipzig -> private Vienna collection (photographed by H.-P. Haack)
licenseBasis: Photographer H.-P. Haack self-published under CC BY 3.0 (own photo of a physical PD-era book object; the photo itself, not the 1915 text, carries this license)
notes: This is the plain cardboard-bound trade issue (spine title + publisher device on front board), not the Ottomar Starke illustrated dust-jacket edition -- no PD/CC-licensed image of the Starke wrapper illustration was found on Commons; candidates only existed on Pinterest/rare-book dealer sites, which are excluded per the brief. Attribution required: 'H.-P. Haack, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.'

licenseTag: CC-PD-Mark / PD-old-70-expired (Commons categories); file page license template = pd
licenseBasis: Commons file page carries the 'pd' license template with UsageTerms=Public domain and AttributionRequired=false; categorized PD-old-70-expired and CC-PD-Mark. This is a photograph of the plain cloth original binding (spine label + front-board title label) of the first edition.
notes: Same photographer/dealer (H.-P. Haack, Antiquariat Dr. Haack Leipzig) as the existing Die Verwandlung cover already in this folder, but this file's own Commons metadata marks it public domain (not CC-BY, unlike the Verwandlung photo and the Strafkolonie photo below) -- verified directly via Commons API extmetadata, not assumed from the pattern.

title: Das Schloss, 1st edition, original paperback wrapper (Kurt Wolff Verlag, Munich, 1926, 502 pages -- Wilpert/Guhring 9; Raabe 9)
sourceCollection: Antiquariat Dr. Haack Leipzig -> private collection, Switzerland (photographed by H.-P. Haack)
licenseBasis: Commons file page rationale (verified via API extmetadata Permission field): the depicted cover is plain typographic text below the threshold of originality ('not a literary work or other protected type'), so it is public domain regardless of the photographer's rights in the photo itself. License template = pd; UsageTerms=Public domain; AttributionRequired=false.
notes: Original paperback wrapper of the first edition (title + publisher device only, no illustration) -- matches the brief's request for the 1926 Kurt Wolff first-edition cover/title page.

licenseBasis: Photographer H.-P. Haack self-published under CC BY 3.0 (verified via Commons API extmetadata: LicenseShortName=CC BY 3.0, AttributionRequired=true, LicenseUrl=creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0). The photo, not the 1919 text, carries this license.
notes: This is the title page (Titelblatt) of the first printing, not a bound-cover photo -- Commons file description explicitly labels it 'Titelblatt des Erstdruckes'. Attribution required: 'H.-P. A separate higher-resolution 68-page PDF scan (File:Kafka In der Strafkolonie (1919).pdf, 2083x3037, 23.2 MB) also exists on Commons but was not used here -- a full-book PDF is out of scope for a single title-page/cover art asset; flagged in case the art pass wants a higher-res crop from that PDF instead.
